entries.note: E38 (spec-entity-fields-12plus.md), first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. plantShield is a long magnitude like arm1/arm2 (extra hit points ahead of the entity's real health pool), so it is priced on the same reference scale those already use: one shield point costs the same as one armor point until a sweep says otherwise.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. LowerIsBetter timer (structural floor, same reason attackInterval has one); referenceScale 1 mirrors stat.derived's own 'one resolver point' scale rather than arm1's, because a countdown in seconds is a much smaller natural range than a hit-point pool.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. A signed delta with no floor (unguarded by design, spec §2b) -- small numbers matter here, so referenceScale 1 keeps a modest adder from pricing as noise.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as attackCountdown: LowerIsBetter timer, structural floor, small natural range.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Most plants never move, so a baseline of zero is ordinary (see StatComposer's own Real() note) -- when it does apply, movement speed is a small natural range, referenceScale 1.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as plantSpeed.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. A long magnitude, priced on arm1/maxHp's own reference scale -- a level-up is a meaningful, discrete magnitude change, not a fractional ratio.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as plantLevel.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Conceptually the same family as the existing 'defense' channel (a flat mitigation stat), so it is priced on defense's own reference scale rather than arm1's hit-point scale.

E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Bearer frame (decided 2026-09-03, spec-entity-fields-12plus.md sec 2c): this channel stays LowerIsBetter, so a RAISE on your OWN takeDmgMultiplier prices as a penalty and a REDUCTION prices as a benefit -- both correct under the bearer frame. takeDmgMultiplier is NOT the authoring surface for 'enemies take more damage': that debuff is a status.apply payload, priced by its own coefficient/trigger/uptime, never a stat.modify on this channel. Reference scale mirrors 'defense' (same damage-mitigation family).
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Mirrors the existing zombieSpeed (uniqueSpeed) channel's own small natural range.
E38, first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result. Same reasoning as zombieSpeedCurrent.

E41 (spec-ui-attach-point.md sec 2c), authored -- not a fitted sweep result, and never will be. A present is read-only: it never writes stat/resource/status/shield/board/currency state, so it is worth exactly zero power, deliberately, in both directions -- a UI atom must not become a free rider that inflates a container's apparent budget, and it must not tax one either. This row exists so CoefficientTable.Find returns an AUTHORED zero (verdict Priced) rather than falling through to the channel-less-row-missing case (verdict unpriced) -- an authored zero and a missing row are different claims, and this row is what keeps them different. Do not delete this row to 'simplify' -- ui.present has PowerCategory.None (AtomKindRegistryTests.cs's own cosmetic exemption), and a missing coefficient here is the exact PLANTED_VIOLATION this module's own pricing test guards against.

E37 (spec-projectile-control.md sec 2c), first-pass -- NOT a fitted sweep result, closing E37's own open criterion 7. bullet.modify has no 'channel' param (its params are op/amount/bulletType/moveWay), so CostFunction reads no channel for it and CoefficientTable.Find is keyed on the channel-less row -- this is that row, not a per-channel one. Reference scale mirrors stat.modify/atk's own precedent (E37's spec cites ("stat.modify", "atk", 1000, 2) as the reference: raw damage is the same unit atk already prices on). op:scale prices off CostFunction.MeanMagnitude's own per-mille mean, same as every other magnitude in this layer -- deliberately under-prices a multiplier over a large base, a known, documented limitation, not this row's to fix.

E44 (spec-power-sweep.md sec 4.1), SWEEP-FITTED 2026-09-05 -- scripts/sweep-power-coefficients.py, corpus data/seed/atoms/generated/family-expand.*.json (45 atoms). CoeffMilli = round(1,000,000 / normalizedMilli(medianFlatMagnitude)) over the atom.mending family's 5 tiers (flat op only -- referenceScale's own contract is 'what one RAW unit means', and 'flat' is the one op whose magnitude is a raw unit; 'increased'/'more' on this same channel are percentage magnitudes this table's (kind,channel) key cannot separately price -- see the script's own FINDING 2, reported not fixed). Result: atom.mending T3 (median tier, mag=74) now prices to 999 instead of 7400, matching atom.might/atom.warding/atom.vitality's own T3 price (999-1000) within rounding -- a measured 3.7x cross-channel spread collapsed to under 0.1%, reproducible by re-running the script. referenceScale (10) is UNCHANGED from the prior authored value -- only CoeffMilli, the dial spec-power-sweep.md names as 'the flat 1000s', was fitted.

E44 (spec-power-sweep.md sec 4.1), SWEEP-FITTED 2026-09-05 -- scripts/sweep-power-coefficients.py, corpus data/seed/atoms/generated/family-expand.*.json (45 atoms). Same fit and same value as the 'hp' row above -- atom.vitality's flat-op magnitudes (24/42/74/130/228) are identical to atom.mending's (hp), so the two channels fit to the same CoeffMilli by construction, not by copy-paste. referenceScale (10) unchanged from the prior authored value.

E44 (spec-power-sweep.md sec 4.1), SWEEP-FITTED 2026-09-05 -- scripts/sweep-power-coefficients.py, corpus data/seed/atoms/generated/family-expand.g-attack.json. CoeffMilli fitted from atom.might's flat-op median (tier 3, mag=9): round(1,000,000 / normalizedMilli(9 at referenceScale 2)) = 222. atom.might T3 now prices to 999, matching the hp/maxHp/defense rows' own T3 price (999-1000) within rounding. atom.ferocity (increased) and atom.savagery (more) share this same channel and coefficient but carry percentage magnitudes (23-435), not raw atk points -- their price is UNCHANGED in ratio terms relative to atom.might (scale-invariant, see the script's FINDING 2); reconciling that needs an `op` axis on this table's key, out of E44's data-only scope. referenceScale (2) unchanged from the prior authored value.

E44 (spec-power-sweep.md sec 4.1), SWEEP-FITTED 2026-09-05 -- scripts/sweep-power-coefficients.py, corpus data/seed/atoms/generated/family-expand.g-armour.json. CoeffMilli fitted from atom.warding's flat-op median (tier 3, mag=4): round(1,000,000 / normalizedMilli(4 at referenceScale 2)) = 500. atom.warding T3 now prices to 1000, matching the atk/hp/maxHp rows' own T3 price (999-1000) within rounding. atom.resilience (increased) shares this channel and carries a percentage magnitude, same FINDING 2 caveat as atk above. referenceScale (2) unchanged from the prior authored value.

Pass-through of CoefficientTable.Authored()'s existing value -- NOT sweep-fitted (no real generated content under data/seed/atoms/ touches arm1 yet; E44's corpus, family-expand, covers only atk/defense/hp/maxHp). Added 2026-09-05 to close a real, independently-verified gap found while fitting the four rows above: RpgStore.GetPowerTables (RpgStore.Power.cs:61-72) falls back to PowerTables.Authored() ONLY when power_coefficient has ZERO rows -- the live dist DB already carries 14 rows from this file's earlier E37/E38/E41 entries, none of which are among Authored()'s original 20, so every one of those 20 (including this one) was SILENTLY UNPRICED in any DB-backed pricing path (ActorPowerCache.Compose skips a missing coefficient rather than pricing it at a flagged zero) the moment this file was first imported -- confirmed live: `SELECT * FROM power_coefficient` against dist/FusionRpg.Server/data/rpg-hot.sqlite returned exactly the 14 rows, none of the 20. This row (and the 15 below) restore the missing 16 as an explicit, unfitted pass-through of the exact value CoefficientTable.Authored() already ships, so importing this file no longer silently drops coverage for channels the sweep had no corpus to fit.
